chapter: Chicago childhood: theaters, violin and first bass
title: Earl Hines at the Grand Terrace and Capone's Cotton Club
summary: Hines had the first big band working in a club at the Grand Terrace, followed by gangster-run Cotton Club in Cicero.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now Earl Hines had a band before the other guys? He had a big band before the other guys? Was he the first to have a big band?
He was the first to have a big band working in a club, yeah.

Yeah. There were a couple of guys that played in a dancehall, a couple of bands that would… not to really note. Jimmy Bell was one that played at the Savoy Ballroom and places like that but Earl Hines got the Grand Terrace, and Ed Fox…

Huge nightclub for that period. We got Earl Hines from Pittsburgh and they got Percy Venable from Pittsburgh also, a great choreographer and they put on a tremendous show. And then the gangsters started. They wanted something for themselves on the west side at Cicero‟s. Al Capone opened up a Cotton Club, which is black entertainment. No black customers of course.
